title: Knowledge Database Coordinator — System Overview
description: The coordinator searches the live JAH Databases manifest — 58,222 databases — by keyword and returns matches with page URLs.
body: The Knowledge / Database Coordinator is the system's memory interface. It loads the live manifest (~/workspace/jah-databases/data/manifest.json, read-only — this project never writes to the clones), scores every database against the query terms across slug, name, tagline, and record kind, and returns ranked matches with their network page URLs. The demonstration runs the coordinator's own stats command against the real manifest: 58,222 databases, load time included. Nothing here is simulated; the manifest is the single source of truth and the coordinator reads it live.

title: Manifest Integrity — The Count Must Match
t: Manifest Integrity — The Count Must Match
description: database_count is cross-checked against actual entries on every load; a mismatch is reported, never hidden.
body: Trust starts with the count. The coordinator compares the manifest's declared database_count with the number of entries actually loaded and reports the boolean. The demonstration runs the integrity check against the live manifest — 58,222 declared, 58,222 loaded, match true — with the real load time in milliseconds.

title: Keyword Search — "calculator"
description: A single keyword returns ranked matches: slug, name, record kind, and page URL.
body: Search splits the query into terms, scores each database (slug hits weigh most, then name, tagline, then full text), and returns the top results. The demonstration searches "calculator" — 167 matches in the live manifest — and prints the top three with their page URLs, exactly as the master coordinator consumes them.

title: Limits and Honest Boundaries
description: The coordinator reads the manifest; it does not fetch live pages, verify record contents, or reach the network.
body: Plain limits. Search results reflect the manifest's metadata — slug, name, tagline — not the live content of each database page; the coordinator never opens a URL. It is read-only over a local file, so a stale local manifest means stale answers, and it knows nothing about databases added after its manifest was written. The demonstration shows a search returning only manifest fields — no page content, no live fetch — proving the boundary is real.

title: Scoring Algorithm — How Matches Are Ranked
t: Scoring Algorithm — How Matches Are Ranked
description: Slug matches weigh 5, name 3, tagline 2, full text 1 — deterministic and explainable.
body: Ranking is arithmetic, not vibes. Each query term adds points per field, and results sort by total score. The demonstration scores two real databases against the term "calculator" and prints the numbers, showing why one outranks the other.
